newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended a nervous day firmer but off its strongest levels on Friday as the market was beset by a plethora of rumours.
At the 1400 GMT close, the rand was pegged at 4.6835/6985 against the dollar from 4.7020/7070 after touching a day's strongest level of 4.6550 bid and a weakest 4.6905 bid.
The currency initially streaked firmer at the opening, gaining almost five cents between 0600 and the 0700 GMT official opening.
Dealers pinned the move on long dollar holders liquidating their positions after Thursday's sharp retracement when the currency gained seven cents from its intraday low.
After dipping below the 4.66 level, however, dealers said local importers and offshore players who sold dollars on the way down, began buying dollars again.
That pushed the currency all the way back up to the 4.69 level, where dealers said the Reserve Bank made an appearance to smooth liquidity.
After stabilising in the 4.68 area, the currency moved in a narrow band for much of the afternoon.
Dealers said trade was stultified on the day by a rash of rumours which spread across the market.

Market talk was that the central bank would announce an interest rate hike on Friday or that the central bank and Finance Ministry were set to announce the abolition of some of the country's remaining exchange controls.
There was also speculation that the Reserve Bank had phoned commercial banks and told them to go home square at the weekend ahead of an announcement on exchange controls.
Senior commercial bank traders said the latter had been flatly denied by the Reserve Bank.
While some traders were convinced there was some truth to the rumours, others labelled them as "guys talking their books".

Finance Departmen spokeswoman Jennifer Wilson said Finance Minister Trevor Manuel did not plan to make any statement after a regular monthly meeting with central bank governor Chris Stals and other Finance Department officials.

A spokesman at the Reserve Bank said Stals planned to attend a private engagement in Cape Town on Friday evening. "As far as I am aware there is no statement planned from the Governor," the spokesman said.
Nevertheless, dealers said market players were reluctant to take any large positions.
"The market was very nervous about having too much of a position in case some form of announcement is made over the weekend," a trader said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.6566/6694 against sterling from 7.6429/6557 overnight and at 0.3242/3246 marks from 0.3217/3222 marks previously.

Bonds were also enthused by the rand's improved performance, as well as stronger U.S. Treasury bonds. In early afternoon trade the benchmark 30-year long bond was pegged at a 6.61 percent yield after settling at 6.64 percent on Thursday.
Dealers said trade was dominated by institutional buying coupled with short-covering at the higher levels and options related selling at the lows.
The key R150 was last quoted at 15.85 percent from 15.93 percent on Thursday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners sold a net 216.12 million rand worth of South African bonds after selling 471.79 million rand worth on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 38.76 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 9.81 billion rand on Wednesday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were slightly higher at between 16.35 and 16.50 percent offered from 16.30 to 16.40 percent previously, while the 90-day BA rate was steady at between 15.85 and 15.70 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 9.69 billion rand on Thursday from 8.667 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
